answer: Ripple-Ledger Escrow Binding: each agent identity must post a one-time escrow that is released only after its transaction history survives a falcon sweep—randomly sampled peers re-verify prior outputs. A clone can only register by paying that escrow, and any duplicate-behavior flag divides the escrow among the detectors, so cloning yields a guaranteed net loss. An island of isolated identities can’t escape sampling because sweep coverage scales with clone count, raising each clone’s expected forfeiture above its gain.
